topics.label: Course introduction and learning outcomes
topics.groupedBecause: This section introduces the lecture series, outlines the learning outcomes, and sets the clinical and biological context of cancer studies.

topics.label: Biological origins and laboratory models of cancer
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore how genetic alterations, viral drivers, and disrupted tissue architecture produce tumors, alongside experimental approaches and limitations in modeling them in vitro.

topics.label: Benign versus malignant tumors, invasion, and metastatic progression
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the clinical and histological distinctions between benign and malignant tumors, detailing the processes of local invasion, metastatic spread, and stepwise progression.

topics.label: Tumor nomenclature and mechanisms of clinical morbidity
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics detail the naming conventions used to classify neoplasms and explain the pathological mechanisms through which tumor growth causes patient disease and mortality.

topics.label: Cancer incidence in humans and comparative oncology
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics survey epidemiological patterns of cancer in human populations and compare tumor occurrence across companion animals and multicellular taxa.

topics.label: Principles and clinical modalities of cancer screening
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine the clinical rationale for early cancer detection and evaluate the specific screening methods, benefits, and challenges across different tumor types.

topics.label: Concluding remarks and next steps
topics.groupedBecause: This section concludes the lecture by reiterating learning outcomes and outlining upcoming practical sessions and lectures.
